correctness.rationale: The 28 noncollinear 2-faces are correctly specified; coning each of seven absent line-triangle boundaries to any one of four off-line points proves integrally that all 1-cycles bound, and dimension count gives free top homology rank 13. Oriented simplicial signed traces follow the Hopf trace identity because no other reduced homology survives. Permutation cycle types and signed face enumeration yield class character (13,-3,1,1,-1,-1), the irreducible character table yields 7+3+conjugate3, and rational transfer yields invariant ranks. The independently executable standard-library program verifies 28 coning identities and 8232 chain-equivariance equalities under all 168 automorphisms. It checks class and cyclic averages, not an infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The classical seven-point binary matroid and its ordinary homology are not claimed new. Inspected Moci–Pezzoli gives a more general equivariant framework but does not supply the six-class character or cyclic quotient numbers of the Fano-matroid independence complex. The closest relevant alternative graph complexes use the seven Fano points or noncollinear triples as graph vertices but different face relations; their claims cannot imply the present matroid-homology character. Searches did not locate an equivalent published class table; this is a provisional priority assessment, not an exhaustive bibliographic certificate.
residual_risks: A complete unindexed or later explicit evaluation of the Fano-matroid homology character may already exist.
The invariant-face-ring literature has not been fully reviewed; the cited 2021 paper is assessed only at abstract level.
The decomposition is over rational/complex coefficients only and does not assert a canonical integral lattice splitting.

value.rationale: The smallest projective binary matroid is a canonical finite geometry; its 168-element symmetry makes its full homology representation a natural test case for equivariant matroid topology. Its ordinary top Betti number 13 cannot determine the unusual mixture of the 7-dimensional and conjugate 3-dimensional irreducibles, nor the fixed ranks of cyclic subgroups. The complete character and quotient profile provide an exact natural invariant beyond routine enumerating of bases.
